editorial:
Imagine meeting your younger self and realizing you were kind of a jerk. That's the fun setup here. Ryan Reynolds plays a time-traveling pilot who crash-lands in 2022 and teams up with his 12-year-old self to fix the future. The movie mixes big action scenes with family drama and plenty of jokes. You get a warm, funny story about growing up, facing grief, and learning to be kinder to yourself. The chemistry between Reynolds and young Walker Scobell feels natural, like real family banter. It's the kind of movie you can watch with your kids or friends and still enjoy the heart behind the laughs.

The action is fast and flashy, with cool jet fights and time-travel effects that look great on a big screen. Reynolds does his usual charming thing, but the emotional moments land harder than expected. The pacing moves quickly, though some jokes feel familiar if you've seen his other films. Still, the story stays engaging. Great for families, sci-fi fans, and anyone wanting an easy, feel-good adventure.
endingExplained: Adam and his younger self team up with their late father, a scientist who helped invent time travel. Together they stop Maya Sorian, the villain who wants to control the future. In the final battle, Adam's dad sacrifices himself to destroy the time machine and save everyone. Adam returns to his own time, now at peace with his past. He visits his younger self and gives him advice, then heads off to a better future with his wife, Laura.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves time-travel adventures with heart and humor.
